# OpenShell as a Security Boundary for Agentic Tool Usage

NVIDIA OpenShell is an open-source runtime (Apache 2.0, launched March 16, 2026)
that enforces security policies on AI coding agents through kernel-level,
out-of-process mechanisms — Landlock LSM, seccomp BPF, and an HTTP CONNECT
proxy with OPA/Rego policy evaluation. This research evaluates whether it
addresses the security gaps identified in the
[security-skills analysis](../security-skills/) and whether it is practical for
a developer workstation and homelab hardware.

## Key Result

| Security Gap | OpenShell Coverage |
|-------------|-------------------|
| Command encapsulation bypass | **Substantially addressed** — kernel enforcement covers all subprocesses |
| Regex evasion | **Substantially addressed** — enforces at syscall/TCP level, not regex |
| TOCTOU | **Partially addressed** — Landlock is continuous; network proxy less certain |
| Data exfiltration | **Partially addressed** — deny-by-default egress; DNS/URL/inference gaps |
| Prompt injection | **Not addressed** — by design; reduces blast radius only |
| Config file weaponization | **Substantially addressed** — filesystem policy protects config paths |

## Decision Framework

1. **Are you running Claude Code with the Anthropic API on a dev workstation?**
   → OpenShell is viable today. Default policy has full Claude Code support.
   No GPU needed. ~2-2.5 GB RAM overhead (est.).

2. **Do you need production-grade isolation?**
   → Not yet. OpenShell is developer preview with no third-party audit. Layer
   with Firecracker/Kata for production.

3. **Is your machine Docker-capable with 4+ GB RAM?**
   → Yes: install and iterate. No: use the `--remote user@host` pattern to
   offload to a homelab server (Intel NUC with 16 GB is ideal).

4. **Do you need multi-agent or multi-model support?**
   → Limited. Single provider-model per gateway. Only Claude Code works
   out-of-box; other agents need custom policies.

5. **Do you need operational governance (skill scanning, audit trails)?**
   → Add Cisco DefenseClaw (open-sourced March 27, 2026) on top of OpenShell.
